title: Scam Texts
about: Never use a surprise text's link: check in the company's own app.

cards.situation: Sam's hoodie is on its way. Then Parcels texts.

image.alt: Sam beside a big phone lock screen at 7:41 with a text from Parcels: We tried to deliver your parcel. Pay a $1.95 fee. Above Sam, a parcel with a tick: the hoodie Sam ordered.

cards.prompt: Sam opens the Parcels thread. **Tap each part** to look closer.

parts.job: Anyone can make a text show a name like Parcels. That's how this one landed in the real thread.
The real Parcels text: no link, just "track it in the Parcels app".
A small fee at a link. Parcel "fees" are a common scam text.
A hurry, so you pay before you think.
parcels-redelivery.example isn't the Parcels app. It's a page anyone could have made.

cards.explanation: The new text asks for money, rushes you and sends you to a strange link.

cards.prompt: Sam taps the link and pays the $1.95 fee. **What happens next?**

image.alt: A pay page at parcels-redelivery.example: Pay $1.95, a card number ending 4821 typed in and the Pay button pressed. Below, three choices: the hoodie arrives; they spend from the card; Parcels refunds it.
image.revealAlt: The card number went to the scammer: Sam's card now shows spending Sam never made, minus $89.00 and minus $240.00. No hoodie is coming.

options.text: They can spend from the card

cards.explanation: The page is the scammer's, so they now have Sam's card number; the $1.95 was just bait.

cards.title: Check the real way
cards.body: A **scam** text copies a name you trust, then rushes you to pay or tap a link. Never use the text's link: check the real way, in the company's own app.

image.alt: The same text, labelled. The sender name Parcels has a grey note: names can be faked. Pay a $1.95 fee: asks for money. Within 2 hours: rushing you. The link parcels-redelivery: fake link. Below, the real Parcels app with an arrow, check here: the hoodie has nothing to pay.

cards.prompt: A new text from Road Tolls. It's a scam. **Tap its three warning signs.**
cards.explanation: It asks for money, rushes you and sends you to a strange link.
cards.nudge: Only the new text counts. Look for money, a hurry and a web address.
cards.showAnswer: The fee, the 12-hour deadline and the link. The sender name could be faked, but you can't see that by looking.

cards.prompt: A text from a new number says it's Alex, Sam's friend. **Tap what Sam should do.**

image.alt: A text from an unknown number, not in Sam's contacts: Hey it's Alex! New number, lost my phone. Can you send me $40 for the train home? Quick pls. Below, three choices: send the $40; reply Is it really you?; call Alex's saved number.
image.revealAlt: Sam calls Alex's saved number. Alex answers: Huh? I'm home. That wasn't me!

options.nudge: The text asks for money and rushes you. What's the real way to reach Alex?
The text asks for money and rushes you. What's the real way to reach Alex?

cards.explanation: There's no app for a friend, so check the real way: the number you already have.
cards.showAnswer: Call Alex's saved number. A reply goes to the new number, which could be the scammer.

cards.prompt: A text says your card from Your Bank is blocked. **Tap where you'd check.**

image.alt: A phone home screen. At the top, a text from Your Bank: Card blocked! Unlock it at yourbank-unlock.example, or call the number we sent. Below, three apps: Messages, to tap the text's link; Phone, to call the text's number; the Your Bank app.

options.nudge: Which of these did the text not give you?
Which of these did the text not give you?

cards.explanation: The app is the real way in; the link and the number came from whoever sent the text.
cards.showAnswer: The Your Bank app. The scammer chose the link and the number, so neither is safe.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
A surprise text with a fee, a rush or a link? Check the real way, in the company's own app.

**Try this:** Find one company text on your phone. Does it want you to tap a link?

**Next:** A call in a voice you know, asking for gift cards.
